info.title: Unlayer API
info.description:
Unlayer API

## Authentication

All endpoints require a Bearer token. Pass it in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-token>
```

Two token types are supported:

| Token | Prefix | Scope | Use case |
|-------|--------|-------|----------|
| **API Key** | `unlayer_sk_` | Project | Server-to-server integration. The project ID is embedded in the key — no `projectId` parameter needed. |
| **Personal Access Token** | `unlayer_pat_` | User | Admin operations. Required for workspace endpoints. Must provide `projectId` via query param or `X-Project-Id` header for project endpoints. |

Most integrations should use an **API Key**. Use a PAT only for workspace management or admin tasks.

> ⚠️ **Server-side use only.** This API does not send CORS headers and cannot be called from a browser. API keys (`unlayer_sk_*`) must never be shipped to client-side code — treat them as secrets.

apiKeyAuth.description: API Key (unlayer_sk_). Project-scoped — the project ID is embedded in the key, so no projectId parameter is needed. Recommended for most integrations.

personalAccessTokenAuth.description: Personal Access Token (unlayer_pat_). User-scoped — required for workspace endpoints and admin operations. Must provide projectId for project endpoints.

get.description: List blocks with cursor-based pagination. Returns both shared project blocks and blocks saved by end-users; each user-saved block carries the userId it was saved under (null for shared blocks), so usage can be aggregated per end-user without enumerating user IDs. Returns blocks in descending order by creation.

parameters.description: The project ID to list blocks for

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Only blocks saved by this end-user (exact match on the user id your app passes to the editor)

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Filter by block ownership: shared project blocks, end-user saved blocks, or both

parameters.name: includeData
parameters.description: Include the block design JSON in each item. Pass false for lightweight sweeps (e.g. usage reports).

isSyncEnabled.description: Whether the block is currently a synced block

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Null if no more results.

has_more.description: Whether there are more results after this page

post.description: Send a transactional email with raw HTML content. The sender domain must be verified in the project workspace; verified sender domains are shared by every Developer Email API project in that workspace.

from.description: Sender email address or "Name <email>" format. Domain must be verified.

to.description: Exactly one recipient. Each request creates one independently tracked delivery.

cc.description: CC is not supported by this endpoint.

bcc.description: BCC is not supported by this endpoint.

text.description: Plain text version of the email. If provided, a multipart/alternative message is sent.

tags.description: Key-value tags for categorizing the email (e.g. {"campaign": "welcome"}). Max 10 tags. Keys (1-64 chars) and values (up to 256 chars) may only contain letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens (the Amazon SES message-tag character set).

headers.description: Custom email headers. Up to 9 printable-ASCII X-* headers are allowed (e.g. {"X-Entity-Ref-ID": "abc123"}). Header names may contain up to 126 characters and each name plus value may contain up to 996 characters.

content.description: Base64-encoded file content. Whitespace and MIME line wrapping are removed before validation; invalid base64 is rejected with a 400 error.

contentType.description: MIME type of the attachment. Required; must be one of the allowed types.

attachments.description: File attachments. Max 10 files per email, max 5 MB total payload size (including headers and base64 overhead).

Returns the current AI credit balance for the project. Credits are pooled per workspace — every project in a workspace shares one balance. Only credit counts are returned; token counts, model names, and costs are never exposed.

reset_date.description: When the current credit period resets, or null if there is no active billing period — including once a subscription is cancelled or its term has ended.

get.description: Returns a project's AI credit exhaustion behavior, alert thresholds, and webhook endpoint. The signing secret is never returned — only whether one exists (`has_signing_secret`).

put.description: Configures AI credit exhaustion behavior, usage alert thresholds, and the webhook endpoint for a project. The HMAC signing secret is generated the first time a webhook URL is set and returned exactly once in the response — store it securely; it is never shown again.

exhaustion_behavior.description: What the editor does when the credit balance is exhausted.

threshold_alerts.description: Usage percentages (1-100) at which a threshold_reached webhook fires, once per crossing per period.

webhook_url.description: HTTPS endpoint that receives AI credit webhooks.

signing_secret.description: The HMAC signing secret. Returned ONLY on the response that first generates it.

post.summary: Rotate the AI credit webhook signing secret.
post.description: Generates a new HMAC signing secret for the project and returns it exactly once. The previous secret stops working immediately, so update your webhook verification before rotating. Requires a webhook URL to be configured first.

signing_secret.description: The new HMAC signing secret. Shown only once.

get.description: Returns AI credit consumption for the project, broken down by end user and feature type. Filterable by date range, end user, and feature type. Usage is updated near real time and grouped by the UTC date when the AI activity occurred. Recent activity may take a short time to appear. Defaults to the current billing period. Only credit counts are returned; token counts, model names, and costs are never exposed. Per-end-user attribution requires the partner to pass `endUserId` on editor initialization.

post.description: Generate or modify an Unlayer design using AI. Send the conversation as `messages` (today only the last user message is consumed; earlier turns are accepted as chat history) and describe the target with `output.kind` + `output.displayMode`. Pass the current canvas state in `context` (full design JSON + selection pointer) to modify an existing design. Only `anthropic` and `openai` models are supported. To import existing HTML or an image instead, use POST /v3/templates/import.

model.description: Preferred AI model in "provider/id" form, e.g. "anthropic/claude-opus-5". Optional — server resolves a default per output kind.

fallbackModels.description: Transient-outage fallback controls. Omit to use Unlayer defaults only when no model is pinned; true always uses Unlayer defaults; false disables the outage tail; an ordered array replaces the default provider/model strings.

image.description: URL or data URL of the image

messages.description: Conversation messages in chronological order, capped at 10 messages. The last `user` message is the prompt for this turn; the newest earlier `user`/`assistant` turns are forwarded within a 12,000-character aggregate history budget. A `user` message may carry a predefined prompt action via `metadata.action.id` (e.g. SPELLING, REPHRASE).

locale.description: BCP-47 fallback locale for AI status messages.

conversationId.description: Reserved for future server-side conversation memory.

model.description: Preferred AI model. Accepts a provider/model string (e.g. "anthropic/claude-opus-5", "openai/gpt-5.6-luna"), a bare provider ("anthropic", "openai") which uses that provider's default model, or a bare model id ("claude-opus-5", "gpt-5.6-luna") with the provider inferred from the name. Optional — defaults to anthropic/claude-opus-5.

fallbackModels.description: Transient-outage fallback controls. Omit to use Unlayer defaults only when no model is pinned; true always uses Unlayer defaults; false disables the outage tail; an ordered array replaces the default provider/model strings.

type.description: The type of input part. "html" or "image" carries the source content; "text" carries optional instructions to apply during import.

data.description: Base64 image data URL, e.g. "data:image/png;base64,…" (for type: "image")

get.description: Returns the canonical design schema as a standard JSON Schema document — the exact schema POST /v3/templates/validate checks against, ready to plug into any JSON Schema validator or editor tooling. Serves the Full schema by default; pass simple=true for the compact Simple schema. No authentication required. Responses carry a strong ETag and long-lived cache headers; send If-None-Match to revalidate for free.

parameters.name: simple
parameters.description: When true, returns the Simple schema instead of the Full schema.

parameters.name: displayMode
parameters.description: Display mode whose rules the schema describes (email, web, document, popup). Defaults to "email".

post.summary: Validate a design against the Unlayer schema.
post.description: Validate a design JSON against the Unlayer design schema. Returns { success: true, data: { valid: true } } when the payload conforms; otherwise data is { valid: false, errors: [...] } with descriptive issues. Every checked design gets HTTP 200 — `data.valid` is the source of truth, not the status code. Only malformed requests (e.g. a missing design field or an unknown displayMode) fail request validation with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

schema.description: Which form of the schema to validate against. Defaults to "full".

displayMode.description: Display mode for the design (email, web, document, popup). Some validation rules differ per mode. Defaults to "email" — without a default, options from every mode would apply at once, the strictest possible check, and real editor-saved designs could be reported invalid.

migrate.description: When true (default), a full-form design with an older schemaVersion is upgraded to the current schema before validating — matching how the editor and the convert endpoints treat stored designs. Designs without a schemaVersion predate versioning and are fully migrated the same way. Set to false to check strict conformance with the current schema version. Designs with a newer schemaVersion than this API knows are validated as-if-current.

customTools.description: Custom tool declarations, in the same shape passed to unlayer.registerTool. When provided, blocks matching a declared tool have their values checked against the tool's declared options (wrong types are reported at their exact path). Blocks of undeclared tools keep envelope-only validation.

migratedFrom.description: Present when the design was upgraded from an older schemaVersion before validation; carries the original version number.

errors.description: Populated when valid is false, capped at 100 entries. Each issue carries the dotted path to the offending field, a human-readable message, and the underlying Zod issue code.

errorCount.description: Total number of issues found; greater than errors.length when the list was capped.

400.description: The request itself is malformed — e.g. the design field is missing or displayMode is unknown. The design was not checked.

schema.description: The request itself is malformed — e.g. the design field is missing or displayMode is unknown. The design was not checked.
